newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel eyes stronger growth after tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Waigel eyes stronger growth after tax reform.

text.p: German finance minister Theo Waigel at the weekend forecast that tax cuts agreed last week could boost German economic growth by 0.5 percentage points.

In a summary of an article to be published in Sunday's edition of Die Welt, Waigel said, "We could count on seeing additional economic growth of some 0.5 percentage points" at the beginning of the tax reform.

Ending months of feuding, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition of Democrats (CDU) and Free Democrats (FDP) on Thursday pledged to cut two points off the so-called solidarity tax to finance German unification, lowering it to 5.5 percent in 1998.
Waigel said the tax breaks totalling between 20 and 30 billion marks would boost investments as well as resuscitate consumer demand.
"Investments could increase by as much as 50 percent."
The cut in the solidarity tax and a reduction of corporate taxes would take effect on January 1, 1998 and the cuts would be financed by commensurate reductions in state spending.
